record.original_question: Can the correspondence between bouncing droplets in vibrating liquids and quantum particles be explained by combining averaging with the Madelung transform?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a viscous incompressible fluid occupying a horizontal bath that is subjected to a periodic vertical vibration, governed by the Navier–Stokes equations with a free surface and the associated continuity equation. Above the resonant Faraday threshold of the bath, small droplets of the same fluid can bounce indefinitely on the vibrating surface and, due to interaction with their self-generated Faraday wave field, propagate horizontally as "walkers." Experimentally, the long-time statistical behavior of such walkers reproduces several hallmarks of quantum mechanics (single- and double-slit diffraction patterns, tunnelling probabilities, quantised orbits in rotating frames, and Anderson-like localisation).

Recall the Madelung transform: for a wave function ψ = √ρ · exp(iS/ℏ) satisfying a Schrödinger-type equation iℏ ∂_t ψ = −(ℏ²/2m) Δψ + Vψ, the pair (ρ, v := ∇S/m) satisfies the continuity equation ∂_t ρ + div(ρ v) = 0 together with a compressible Euler-type equation with an additional "quantum pressure" (Bohm potential) term −(ℏ²/2m) Δ(√ρ)/√ρ. Recall also the method of averaging for fast/slow dynamical systems, in which one replaces a system with rapidly oscillating coefficients by an effective system obtained by integrating over the fast phase.

Problem. Construct a rigorous mathematical procedure that, starting from the free-boundary hydrodynamic system describing a droplet bouncing on a vertically vibrated fluid bath (a system with rapidly time-periodic forcing and a domain whose topology changes once per bouncing period), produces—after an appropriate averaging over the fast bouncing/Faraday timescale—an effective slow system that can be put, via the Madelung transform, into the form of a Schrödinger-type equation governing the statistical behavior of the droplet's position. Equivalently, derive (or prove the impossibility of deriving) the empirically observed quantum-like statistics of walking droplets as the result of combining an averaging principle for the underlying fluid equations with the Madelung correspondence between compressible hydrodynamics and quantum mechanics.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of explaining the walker–quantum correspondence by combining averaging with the Madelung transform is posed as an open problem in geometric hydrodynamics. Existing literature (Bush–Oza reviews, Bohmian and Nelsonian re-derivations, and works on the Madelung transform) discuss the analogy and partial heuristic links, but no rigorous derivation via averaging plus Madelung is known. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic quantum analogs (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of walking droplets exhibiting quantum-like behavior; no rigorous averaging+Madelung derivation given.
status_evidence.claim: A complete derivation of the quantum analogy from the underlying hydrodynamics is not available.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of the Madelung transform
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the geometric/symplectic structure of the Madelung transform between hydrodynamics and Schrödinger equations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the Madelung side of the proposed program but does not include the averaging step from droplet dynamics.

status_evidence.title: What can bouncing oil droplets tell us about quantum mechanics?
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses limits of the walker–quantum analogy and lack of a rigorous link.
status_evidence.claim: Supports that a rigorous explanation of the analogy is still missing.
